basis: Neurodegeneration defines this storage disease; dysostosis in 3/3 and hearing loss in 80-99%. Skin disease omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone does not prove liver dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive neurologic deterioration is a defining feature of fucosidosis, supported by regression, CNS hypomyelination and intellectual disability.

basis: Mitochondrial optic atrophy; deafness and myopathy each 30-79%. Impaired neuromuscular transmission (30-79%) omitted at cap; neuropathy and ataxia only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: none at cap: impaired neuromuscular transmission occurs in 30-79%, but deafness and myopathy are more characteristic; neuropathy and ataxia occur in 5-29%.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an inherited mitochondrial disease affecting cellular energy metabolism.

basis: Neurocutaneous pigmentary mosaicism; structural skeletal abnormalities occur in roughly 30-50%. Ocular abnormalities are less consistently above 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital skeletal abnormalities, including scoliosis, limb asymmetry and digit malformations, affect roughly 30-50%; estimates vary by series.

basis: Congenital cerebral clefts cause neurologic dysfunction; strabismus in 80-99% reflects impaired alignment and does not establish direct ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent strabismus can arise from cerebral motor dysfunction; it does not establish direct damage to the eye.

basis: Craniotubular skeletal dysplasia with characteristic dental hypoplasia in its definition. Proptosis and curly hair alone do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic dental hypoplasia is part of the defined syndrome; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Narcolepsy type 1 entails loss of hypothalamic orexin neurons, usually attributed to immune-mediated destruction. Autonomic symptoms do not establish other organ damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: typical narcolepsy type 1 is regarded as immune-mediated loss of orexin neurons; rare inherited forms do not define the umbrella's usual mechanism.

basis: Down syndrome causes neurodevelopmental impairment; congenital heart defects ~40-50%, hearing impairment ~50-75%, and functional ocular abnormalities >50%.

decisions.ocular: involved: developmental ocular abnormalities causing refractive or visual dysfunction affect >50%; these are common syndromic manifestations.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects ~50-75%, commonly with abnormal external/middle-ear development and persistent conductive dysfunction.

basis: Defining hyaline infiltration affects skin, larynx and oral mucosa. Dystonia is reported in 30-79%, supporting neurologic dysfunction; calcification alone would not qualify.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: characteristic early hoarseness reflects direct laryngeal infiltration; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal and gingival infiltration with tongue nodules is a defining mucocutaneous manifestation.
decisions.neurologic: involved: dystonia is annotated as frequent (30-79%), supporting functional CNS involvement rather than asymptomatic calcification alone.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: the historical lipid-metabolism classification is misleading; ECM1-related extracellular matrix deposition is not an established metabolic or endocrine defect.

basis: Inborn bile acid synthesis/conjugation defect with neonatal cholestasis; fat malabsorption results from deficient bile acids rather than direct intestinal damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: fat malabsorption reflects inadequate luminal bile acids; direct intestinal injury or intrinsic intestinal dysfunction is not established.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; developmental delay/pyramidal dysfunction, optic atrophy and hearing impairment each occur in 2/2 reported patients.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay and pyramidal dysfunction occur in 2/2 patients; they are consequences of the defining respiratory-chain metabolic defect.
